entities.name: Hanno the Elder
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Hanno the Elder was a Carthaginian general serving under Mago Barca in the Second Punic War, a key figure in the North African campaigns of the Punic Wars. Born in Carthage during the 3rd century BCE, Hanno led the expedition to the western coast of Africa, which included the modern-day countries of Morocco and Western Sahara. This voyage was a major achievement for Carthage, expanding its influence in the region and securing crucial resources.

The expedition also had significant cultural and historical implications, as it marked one of the earliest recorded instances of a European expedition to the Atlantic coast of Africa. The voyage's legacy can be seen in the subsequent exploration and colonization of the Americas by European powers.

Despite the significance of Hanno's expedition, the general's own legacy has been somewhat overshadowed by that of his contemporary, Hanno, son of Bomilcar. Nevertheless, Hanno the Elder's contributions to Carthaginian military strategy and his role in shaping the course of the Punic Wars remain an important part of historical record.

Hanno's story serves as a reminder of the complex and multifaceted nature of historical events, highlighting the importance of nuanced understanding and contextual analysis in reconstructing the past.
